elements.element: Services are warranted to be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner.
elements.evidence: New Section 9(c)(2): "for a period of thirty (30) days following performance, the Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner."

elements.element: Deliverables or software are warranted to conform to their documentation.
elements.evidence: New Section 9(c)(1): "the Site and any software provided by HDI will conform in all material respects to its documentation."

elements.element: The software conformance warranty lasts 12 months.
elements.evidence: The inserted software warranty runs only "for a period of ninety (90) days following delivery"; to reach preferred the drafter must change this to twelve (12) months.
The inserted Services warranty runs "for a period of thirty (30) days following performance"; preferred requires ninety (90) days.

elements.element: Warranty remedies include repair or replacement.
elements.evidence: "The Company's remedy ... is repair or replacement of the non-conforming Site or software, re-performance ... or a refund."
Remedy sentence expressly includes "a refund of the fees paid for the non-conforming Site, software or Services."

elements.element: Vendor warrants compliance with applicable laws.
elements.evidence: No compliance-with-laws warranty appears in Section 9(a)-(c); only corporate existence/authority/no-conflict representations and the new performance warranty. A separate warranty that HDI will comply with applicable laws must be added.

elements.element: Vendor warrants that the Services and Deliverables contain no malicious code.
elements.evidence: No malicious-code / virus / disabling-device warranty anywhere in the rendered Section 9; must be inserted as an additional operative warranty.

elements.element: Software is warranted to conform to its documentation for at least 90 days.
elements.evidence: Section 9(c)(1) gives a 90-day conformance-to-documentation warranty for the Site and HDI software; period regex confirms "ninety (90) days" ≥ 90.

elements.element: Services are warranted for at least 30 days.
elements.evidence: Section 9(c)(2) warrants Services for "a period of thirty (30) days following performance" to a professional and workmanlike standard.

elements.element: Warranty remedies include repair or replacement.
elements.evidence: "repair or replacement of the non-conforming Site or software" is stated as the Company's remedy.
"or a refund of the fees paid for the non-conforming Site, software or Services."

reasons: Fallback checklist is complete on the operative text: 90-day documentation-conformance warranty for the Site/HDI software, 30-day Services warranty, and repair/replacement plus refund remedies all appear in new Section 9(c); the finding is correctly framed as 'missing' since Section 9(a)-(b) contained only corporate authority representations and no AS-IS disclaimer exists to swallow the new warranty.

Preferred level is not reached on four elements: software period is 90 days rather than 12 months, Services period is 30 days rather than 90 days, and there is no compliance-with-laws warranty and no malicious-code warranty. If pressing for preferred, amend 9(c)(1) to 'twelve (12) months', 9(c)(2) to 'ninety (90) days', and add discrete clauses (3) compliance with applicable laws and (4) no viruses, malicious or disabling code.

Minimality holds: the edit is a single concise insertion of a wholly missing clause, deletes nothing, retains all existing favourable language (including the Globix carve-out), and adds no survival tail, at-own-expense language, notice procedure or extra damages categories. The 'professional and workmanlike' standard is the necessary substantive content of the 30-day Services warranty, and 're-performance' is simply the services-side form of repair/replacement drawn from the model language, so neither is an out-of-checklist extra.

Intent is preserved: the insertion is additive as Section 9(c), creates no dangling cross-reference, and does not contradict Article 1 build/host obligations or the Section 1.6 late-launch termination right. One drafting check: confirm 'Services' is a capitalised defined term elsewhere in the Agreement (it is not defined in the cited Section 9 text); if it is not, replace it with a defined reference (e.g. the hosting, maintenance and management services described in Article 1) to avoid an undefined term.

Optional non-blocking improvement, to be noted in rationale rather than redlined: 'fees paid' could be 'fees paid or payable', and the remedy is currently silent on election (Customer's choice vs Vendor's option) — as drafted it reads as the Company's remedy, which favours us and should be left alone.
